description: Graduate machine learning with the theory behind generalisation and the major families of methods beyond the introductory course: kernels, boosting, Bayesian models, representation learning, bandits, and learning with limited labels. Students derive key results, implement the methods from scratch in the lab, and reproduce and critique a published result.
modelledOn: Shalev-Shwartz and Ben-David, Understanding Machine Learning: From Theory to Algorithms
Murphy, Probabilistic Machine Learning: An Introduction and Advanced Topics
Hastie, Tibshirani and Friedman, The Elements of Statistical Learning
Rasmussen and Williams, Gaussian Processes for Machine Learning
outcomes: Derive generalisation bounds from the PAC, VC and Rademacher frameworks and explain what they do and do not guarantee.
Implement and analyse kernel machines, boosted ensembles and Gaussian process models from first principles.
Apply approximate Bayesian inference with the Laplace approximation, variational methods and Markov chain sampling.
Learn low-dimensional and self-supervised representations and judge their quality.
Design online, bandit, active and transfer learning solutions and bound their regret or label cost.
Reproduce a published result with statistical rigour and report calibration, uncertainty and failure modes.

units.title: Statistical learning and generalisation
topics: Empirical risk minimisation, true risk and the generalisation gap
PAC learning and sample complexity for finite hypothesis classes
VC dimension and Rademacher complexity; uniform convergence
Bias-variance decomposition and double descent
Regularisation, structural risk minimisation and implicit bias of gradient descent
Cross-validation, model selection and honest evaluation with nested splits

units.title: Kernel methods and support vector machines
topics: Maximum margin classification: primal and dual SVM
Kernels, Mercer's theorem and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces
Soft margins, hinge loss and sequential minimal optimisation
Kernel ridge regression and kernel PCA
Scaling kernels: random Fourier features and the Nystrom approximation

units.title: Ensembles and boosting
topics: Bagging, random forests and out-of-bag error
AdaBoost, exponential loss and margin theory
Gradient boosting as functional gradient descent
Regularised second-order boosting with histogram splits
Stacking, diversity and why ensembles generalise

units.title: Bayesian methods and Gaussian processes
topics: Bayesian linear regression: conjugate priors and the posterior predictive
Gaussian processes: kernels as priors over functions, posterior and prediction
Marginal likelihood and hyperparameter learning
Approximate inference: Laplace approximation and variational inference
Markov chain Monte Carlo: Metropolis-Hastings and Hamiltonian Monte Carlo
Bayesian optimisation with acquisition functions

units.title: Dimensionality reduction and representation learning
topics: PCA via the singular value decomposition and probabilistic PCA
Independent components and sparse coding with dictionaries
Manifold learning: spectral embeddings, t-SNE and the idea behind UMAP
Autoencoders and variational autoencoders with the evidence lower bound
Self-supervised and contrastive representation learning

units.title: Online learning and bandits
topics: Regret and online gradient descent
Prediction with expert advice: weighted majority and Hedge
Multi-armed bandits: epsilon-greedy, UCB and Thompson sampling
Contextual bandits and linear upper confidence bounds
Application: adaptive advice for smallholder farmers or mobile-money fraud rules

units.title: Semi-supervised, active and transfer learning
topics: Self-training, consistency regularisation and label propagation
Active learning: uncertainty sampling and query by committee
Transfer learning: fine-tuning and domain adaptation
Distribution shift: covariate shift, importance weighting and detection
Learning with few labels in low-resource languages and sensor data
Calibration and conformal prediction for reliable uncertainty

units.title: Research practice in machine learning
topics: Reproducing a published result: seeds, hyperparameters and discrepancy diagnosis
Ablations and statistical comparison of learning algorithms across datasets
Fairness, robustness and responsible deployment checks
Project report: a method, an experiment and a critical discussion

schedule.title: Risk, PAC learning and capacity
schedule.exercise: Derive the sample size needed to learn a finite hypothesis class to error 0.05 with 95 percent confidence, and compute the VC dimension of intervals on the line.

tasks.title: Fit polynomials of degree 1 to 12 on 20 points, plot training and test error against degree, and mark the generalisation gap
Plot the PAC sample-size bound against hypothesis class size and tolerance, then check it against the error of a learner on simulated data
Estimate the empirical Rademacher complexity of threshold classifiers and linear classifiers on random samples, and compare it with the observed generalisation gap

schedule.title: Bias, variance, regularisation and evaluation
schedule.exercise: Decompose the expected squared error of a ridge regression into bias, variance and noise, and design a nested cross-validation protocol for choosing the penalty.

tasks.title: Simulate 200 training sets, fit models of three complexities, and estimate bias and variance at five test points from the spread of predictions
Sweep the ridge penalty on a 60-feature dataset, plot validation error and coefficient paths, and pick the penalty by cross-validation
Fit random-feature regression with growing width past the interpolation point, plot test error, and reproduce the double descent curve

schedule.title: Maximum margin and kernels
schedule.exercise: Derive the dual of the hard-margin SVM, identify the support vectors in a 2D example, and show that a polynomial kernel corresponds to an explicit feature map.

tasks.title: Plot the maximum margin line for 10 separable 2D points, mark the support vectors, and verify that moving a non-support point does not change it
Train an SVM with linear, polynomial and Gaussian kernels on a ring-shaped dataset and compare the decision boundaries and test accuracy
Implement a simplified sequential minimal optimisation solver for a soft-margin SVM and verify its dual objective against a library solver

schedule.title: Kernel regression and scaling kernels
schedule.exercise: Show that kernel ridge regression solution lies in the span of the training points, and compare the cost of exact kernels with random features for a million samples.

tasks.title: Fit kernel ridge regression with a Gaussian kernel to 30 noisy points and plot fits for three bandwidths and penalties
Apply kernel PCA to a two-spirals dataset, plot the top components, and compare with linear PCA for separating the two classes
Approximate a Gaussian kernel with random Fourier features, measure approximation error against feature count, and time it against the exact method on 20000 points

schedule.title: Bagging and boosting
schedule.exercise: Derive the AdaBoost weight update from exponential loss, and write gradient boosting for squared error as repeated fitting of residuals.

tasks.title: Train a random forest on a crop-yield classification dataset, compare out-of-bag error with test error, and plot error against the number of trees
Step through five rounds of AdaBoost with decision stumps on 10 points, showing the weight update and the combined classifier after each round
Implement gradient boosting with shallow trees for squared and logistic loss from scratch and compare with a library model on held-out data

schedule.title: Bayesian regression and Gaussian processes
schedule.exercise: Derive the posterior and predictive distribution of Bayesian linear regression with a Gaussian prior, and show how the Gaussian process predictive follows from conditioning.

tasks.title: Update a Bayesian linear regression one data point at a time and plot the posterior over the line and the predictive band after 0, 1, 5 and 20 points
Sample functions from a Gaussian process prior with two kernels, condition on 8 observations, and plot the posterior mean and uncertainty band
Fit length scale and noise by maximising the marginal likelihood on a rainfall time series, and compare with cross-validated choices

schedule.title: Approximate inference and Bayesian optimisation
schedule.exercise: Compare the Laplace approximation and a mean-field variational fit to a skewed posterior, and write the acquisition function for expected improvement.

tasks.title: Fit a Laplace approximation to the posterior of a logistic regression coefficient and overlay it on the exact posterior computed on a grid
Implement Metropolis-Hastings for a two-parameter posterior, tune the step size, and report acceptance rate, trace plots and effective sample size
Tune two hyperparameters of a classifier with Bayesian optimisation and compare 20 evaluations against 20 random search evaluations over 10 repeats

schedule.title: Linear representations
schedule.exercise: Show that PCA directions are the top singular vectors of the centred data matrix, and explain when independent components differ from principal components.

tasks.title: Compute PCA of a 5-feature dataset through the SVD, plot the explained variance, and decide how many components keep 90 percent
Mix three known sound signals with a random matrix, recover them with independent component analysis, and measure the correlation with the originals
Embed a 1000-point image digit dataset with PCA, t-SNE and a spectral embedding, compare neighbourhood preservation, and show how perplexity changes t-SNE

schedule.title: Autoencoders and self-supervised learning
schedule.exercise: Derive the evidence lower bound of a variational autoencoder and explain the roles of the reconstruction and KL terms.

tasks.title: Watch a small autoencoder train on 2D points, and plot reconstruction error against code size of 1, 2 and 3 units
Train a variational autoencoder on small digit images, sample new images from the prior, and plot the effect of the KL weight
Pre-train an encoder with a contrastive loss on unlabelled images, then train a linear classifier on 100 labels and compare with training from scratch

schedule.title: Online learning and bandits
schedule.exercise: Prove the sublinear regret of online gradient descent for convex losses, and compare the regret curves of epsilon-greedy, UCB and Thompson sampling.

tasks.title: Simulate a 5-arm bandit with epsilon-greedy for 2000 steps over 100 runs and plot average reward and the share of optimal pulls
Run weighted majority and Hedge with 10 experts on a prediction sequence, and plot cumulative regret against the best expert
Implement linear UCB to recommend one of 6 fertiliser plans from field features, simulate 5000 rounds, and plot cumulative regret against a fixed-plan baseline

schedule.title: Learning with few labels
schedule.exercise: Compare the label budget needed by random and uncertainty-based querying on a pool of 5000 points, and explain when self-training reinforces its own mistakes.

tasks.title: Run label propagation on a two-moons dataset with 2 labelled points per class and plot the labels it assigns to the rest
Compare random sampling, uncertainty sampling and query by committee on a text classification pool by plotting accuracy against labels used
Fine-tune a pre-trained image model from one crop type to another with 50 target labels, and compare frozen features, full fine-tuning and scratch training

schedule.title: Shift, few-shot data and calibrated uncertainty
schedule.exercise: Show how importance weighting corrects covariate shift, and construct a conformal prediction set with 90 percent coverage on a calibration split.

tasks.title: Plot a reliability diagram for a classifier on 2000 test points, compute the expected calibration error, and fix it with temperature scaling
Train a classifier where the test inputs come from a shifted distribution, detect the shift with a domain classifier, and reweight to recover accuracy
Build split conformal prediction sets for a regression model, check coverage over 50 random splits, and show how set width varies with difficulty

schedule.title: Reproduction, ablation and project report
schedule.exercise: Write the discrepancy report for a reproduced result, listing every difference from the paper, its likely effect, and the check you ran.

tasks.title: Re-run a given training script with 10 random seeds, report mean and standard deviation of test accuracy, and compare with the single number claimed
Compare three learning algorithms on 8 datasets with a paired test and a rank-based test, and report which differences survive correction for multiple testing
Reproduce a published learning method on a new dataset, run ablations and a fairness check across groups, and write a critical project report
